quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only when needed to avoid a crash. Do not use it to tell slow drivers to speed up or move out of your way.

questions.question: A bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Problems controlling your vehicle.
Brakes to squeal.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Problems controlling your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives a smooth ride. If your vehicle bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when can you move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog, rain, or snow?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back in these conditions and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: What should you do before passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may seem slower than they really are. Only pass if you are sure you can safely change lanes. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass.

questions.question: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm out, you must stay completely stopped until the lights turn off, the stop arm goes in, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Keep track of traffic in front of you and in the lane next to you.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter to claim your right-of-way.
Wait until you can get completely across before entering.
Go into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can get completely across before entering.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection is illegal.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive through the intersection without stopping.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic light or stop sign, what should you do first?

options.text: Press the accelerator pedal hard.
Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors first to see what traffic is near you. Release the accelerator to slow down. Move your foot to the brake and press steadily for a smooth stop.

questions.question: How can you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to see where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that right turns are not allowed at this intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you to watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked car.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note attached to the vehicle you hit. Include your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Always buckle your safety belt before starting the engine. Ask all passengers to buckle theirs as well.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
Merge across two lanes at once.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Find a gap large enough to safely enter the flow of traffic. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps available.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, in rain, or in snow, visibility is poor. How can you best let other drivers know you are there?

options.text: Turn up the dashboard lights.
Turn on your parking lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see clearly or when other drivers may not see you. Use low beams when weather or darkness requires you to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Tap your brakes, then resume your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to pass you.
questions.explanation: If possible, change lanes. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to give more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car or from between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their vehicle before seeing you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly or without planning.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly or without planning.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, make sure no vehicles are in the space you want to enter. Check your mirrors and blind spots. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes to give other drivers time to react.

questions.question: "Implied consent" means:

options.text: You must take a chemical test to measure your blood alcohol level (BAC).
You will take a field sobriety test to check for impairment.
You will have a physical exam before getting your license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must take a chemical test to measure your blood alcohol level (BAC).
questions.explanation: By driving on a Maryland roadway, you agree to take a test that measures alcohol or other drugs in your blood. The MVA will suspend your license if you take the test and have a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

questions.question: You can help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Driving at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: It is hard to keep a safe distance behind your vehicle. You can help by driving at a steady speed and signaling your turns, lane changes, and slowing down in advance.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that pedestrians may be crossing ahead. If a pedestrian is crossing in the crosswalk, you must stop and wait until they are no longer in the crosswalk.
